owner_rules: Done means ALL evidence: implemented as specified (task id), a test that FAILED before and passes now, suites green, measured number vs target, docs regenerated, committed AND pushed to the contract's branch.
Never defer: no "later", "follow-up", "out of scope". If blocked: what blocks, what you tried, what you need; then continue with the next task.
Root cause, then fix: file:line + mechanism. No weakening tests, raising timeouts, skips, relaxed assertions.
No silent scope cuts: never lower targets, caps or test sizes without owner approval.
Never bypass guards: no --no-verify, no bypass env vars, no skip flags.
Deliver continuously: one task per commit, pushed to the contract's branch as it goes green.
Honest reporting: TASK-ID | status | commit | tests | measured vs target | missing.

tasks.title: Unrebuildable notes are counted and surfaced
requirements: recover() records every path it cannot rebuild with the reason (content hash mismatch, record unreadable) instead of continuing silently
status() reports unrecoverable with the paths, and memev doctor has an oplog check that fails naming them
DESIGN.md and THREAT-MODEL.md say what is rebuilt and what is reported

an unrebuildable path is detected at open and before every later write to it (append, remember, checkpoint, journal, sync after a pull), so a later write never logs the loss as an external delete; the doctor's drift fix never deletes or overwrites such a path
the finding is shown where people look: the human memev status line and the session card name the count and point at memev doctor, and the CLI doctor shows the check with the daemon up or down
status() and the MCP status and doctor tools list an unrecoverable path only to a token whose path scope covers it; other callers see the count
when the vault has a git backup, the doctor names the last backup commit that held the lost path as the recovery source

a write, append, remember, checkpoint, journal turn or sync to an unrebuildable path is refused with a VaultError whose code is unrecoverable and whose message points at memev doctor; nothing is logged for it, whether the file is missing, incomplete or unreadable

the doctor names, as the recovery source, the newest backup commit that still holds the path (the deletion commit never), reading git directly when the daemon is down; with no backup, memev doctor --resolve <path> ends the report only after a confirmation, by logging a delete of the path with the reason

the unrecoverable list is computed at each open from the log and the disk, plus the paths a damaged line was found to break: when open() meets a line it cannot apply, it records that path and the reason in .memev/unrecoverable.json (never in the log), so the report survives the next snapshot; a path leaves the list once its file holds the bytes its head expects or --resolve ends it; a healthy note whose file is removed is rebuilt from the log at open, as before; a path that compact() archived is never reported

status(), memev_status, memev_doctor, memev_session_start and POST /v1/session-start name an unrecoverable path only to a token whose path scope covers it; other callers, remote connectors included, see the count
the rendered session card text, the MCP text, memev card and plain memev status carry the count and 'memev doctor' in their first lines, so the card's 6000-character cut never drops them
the oplog check lists unrecoverable paths whether or not verify() is ok

a record that parses as JSON but cannot be applied (data null, a splice whose ins is not an array, a put whose content is not a string, a line that is not an object) is treated as unreadable; Vault.open() never throws because of one path
iterate() reports a line it cannot parse with its segment and offset, and materialize attributes it to the path whose chain it breaks, so each path gets its own reason

a present file whose bytes equal any state of the note that verifies (the head after any record whose hash checks, the named backup commit's copy included) clears the report and is imported as one outside edit; a present file that is a strict prefix of the last verified content, or of the content the log holds even when it fails its hash, is incomplete and kept as it is; any other present file is an outside edit and is imported
docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md's oplog row names the note-cannot-be-rebuilt failure and its recovery from the named backup commit

memev doctor --resolve <path> asks for confirmation on a terminal and needs --yes otherwise; it refuses a path that is not unrecoverable or skipped, acts by the path's state (for an unrecoverable path it ends the report as requirement 9 says; for a path SR-1.26 skips it moves the note as SR-1.26 says), and goes through the daemon when it is running
the oplog check's detail, verify() errors included, names a path only to a token whose path scope covers it; other callers see counts
the unrecoverable refusal runs after the caller's access check, so a caller without access to the path gets the access refusal, never 'unrecoverable'
the git-pull loop in src/cli/sync.mjs catches the unrecoverable refusal per path, keeps the path reported and goes on; the pull still commits and pushes the other paths
every caller of status() passes the caller's identity, src/server/http.mjs included, so requirement 11's scope rule holds on every route
